cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Colossal Head (Olmec)
Date: ca. 900-400 BCE
Period/Culture: Olmec (Formative/Preclassic)
Location: La Venta, Tabasco, Mexico
Medium: Basalt (about 9 ft tall)
Fact: Likely a portrait of a ruler in a helmet; multi-ton boulder hauled 50+ miles with no wheels or draft animals.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: El Castillo (Pyramid of Kukulcán)
Date: ca. 800-900 CE
Period/Culture: Maya (Terminal Classic, Maya-Toltec)
Location: Chichén Itzá, Yucatán, Mexico
Medium: Limestone
Fact: A stone calendar: 91 steps × 4 sides + top platform = 365; equinox shadows form a serpent sliding down the north stairs.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Coatlicue
Date: ca. 1500 CE
Period/Culture: Mexica/Aztec (Late Postclassic)
Location: Tenochtitlan (Mexico City); now Museo Nacional de Antropología
Medium: Andesite (about 11.5 ft tall)
Fact: Mother of Huitzilopochtli; decapitated, blood streams out as two serpents forming her face; necklace of hands and hearts, skirt of snakes.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Purse cover, Sutton Hoo ship burial
Date: ca. 625 CE
Period/Culture: Early Medieval / Anglo-Saxon
Location: Suffolk, England; now British Museum
Medium: Gold, garnet, and glass cloisonné
Fact: Royal ship burial, likely King Raedwald of East Anglia; man between two beasts and eagles attacking ducks; matches treasure burials in Beowulf.
cards.search: Purse cover, Sutton Hoo ship burial

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Chi-Rho-Iota (XPI) page, Book of Kells
Date: ca. 800 CE
Period/Culture: Early Medieval / Hiberno-Saxon
Location: Probably Iona, Scotland, then Kells, Ireland; now Trinity College Dublin
Medium: Tempera (pigment) on vellum
Fact: XPI = first Greek letters of "Christ"; opens Matthew 1:18 (Christ's birth); cats and mice hidden in the interlace; made in a scriptorium.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Virgin and Child (Morgan Madonna)
Date: ca. 1150-1200
Period/Culture: Romanesque
Location: Auvergne, France; now Metropolitan Museum of Art, NY
Medium: Painted wood (walnut)
Fact: A Throne of Wisdom: Mary is the throne, Christ is divine wisdom; stiff and frontal; carried in processions.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Bayeux Tapestry
Date: ca. 1070-1080
Period/Culture: Romanesque (Norman)
Location: Probably made in England; kept in Bayeux, France
Medium: Embroidered wool on linen (about 230 ft long, 20 in high)
Fact: Not a tapestry, it's embroidery; tells the Norman Conquest and Battle of Hastings (1066); shows Halley's Comet.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Abbey church of Saint-Denis
Date: ca. 1140-1144 (choir)
Period/Culture: Gothic (Early), French
Location: Saint-Denis, near Paris, France
Medium: Stone architecture with stained glass
Fact: Abbot Suger's choir is the first Gothic building; rib vaults and pointed arches open walls to glass for lux nova; burial church of French kings.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Virgin of Jeanne d'Évreux
Date: 1324-1339
Period/Culture: Gothic (Late), French
Location: Paris; given to Saint-Denis; now the Louvre
Medium: Silver gilt, basse-taille enamel, gold, crystal, pearls
Fact: Luxury art and a reliquary (fleur-de-lis scepter held relics of Mary); Queen Jeanne d'Évreux gave it to Saint-Denis in 1339; S-curve sway.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Röttgen Pietà
Date: ca. 1300-1325
Period/Culture: Gothic (Late), German
Location: Rhineland, Germany; now Rheinisches Landesmuseum, Bonn
Medium: Painted wood
Fact: Private devotional image (Andachtsbild); emaciated Christ with grape-like wounds, made grotesque so the viewer shares Mary's grief.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Lamentation — Giotto di Bondone
Date: ca. 1305
Period/Culture: Late Gothic / Proto-Renaissance, Italian
Location: Arena (Scrovegni) Chapel, Padua, Italy
Medium: Fresco
Fact: Diagonal rock ledge leads your eye to Christ's face; figures with backs to viewer give weight and stage-like space; weeping angels.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Gates of Paradise (east doors, Baptistery) — Lorenzo Ghiberti
Date: 1425-1452
Period/Culture: Early Italian Renaissance
Location: Baptistery of San Giovanni, Florence
Medium: Gilded bronze relief
Fact: 10 Old Testament panels using linear perspective in relief; Michelangelo reportedly named them; Ghiberti put his self-portrait in the frame.
cards.search: Gates of Paradise (east doors, Baptistery) — Lorenzo Ghiberti

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: David — Donatello
Date: ca. 1440-1460
Period/Culture: Early Italian Renaissance
Location: Medici palace courtyard, Florence; now the Bargello
Medium: Bronze (about 5 ft 2 in)
Fact: First freestanding life-size nude male statue since antiquity; contrapposto; shepherd's hat, standing on Goliath's head; Medici symbol of Florence.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Primavera — Sandro Botticelli
Date: ca. 1482
Period/Culture: Early Italian Renaissance
Location: Florence (Medici commission); now the Uffizi
Medium: Tempera on wood panel
Fact: Venus in an orange grove with Cupid, Three Graces, Mercury, Flora, and Zephyrus chasing Chloris; Humanist/Neoplatonic allegory of love and spring.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Last Supper — Leonardo da Vinci
Date: ca. 1495-1498
Period/Culture: High Renaissance
Location: Refectory, Santa Maria delle Grazie, Milan
Medium: Oil and tempera on plaster (a secco)
Fact: Moment after "one of you will betray me"; Christ's head is the vanishing point, apostles in groups of three; a secco made it flake within decades.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: David — Michelangelo Buonarroti
Date: 1501-1504
Period/Culture: High Renaissance
Location: Florence; now Galleria dell'Accademia
Medium: Marble (about 17 ft)
Fact: Carved from an abandoned block; shows David before the fight, tense and alert; civic symbol of the Florentine Republic.

cards.front: Identify this work: name, date, culture, location, medium, one fact
cards.back:
Name: Melencolia I — Albrecht Dürer
Date: 1514
Period/Culture: Northern Renaissance, German
Location: Nuremberg, Germany
Medium: Engraving
Fact: Winged genius sits idle among tools, stuck between inspiration and inaction; magic square rows add to 34 and hide the date 1514.
